newsitem.title: USA: Northeast says nuclear license not under threat.
newsitem.headline: Northeast says nuclear license not under threat.

text.p: Northeast Utilities said Friday its license to operate the Millstone 1 nuclear plant in Waterford, Conn., was not threatened by a ruling by federal regulators late on Thursday.
The federal Nuclear Regulatory Commission said on Thursday that Northeast had violated minor procedures during refueling at its Millstone plants but did not jeopardise public safety.

The agency said the preliminary ruling was in response to a 1995 petition filed by former Northeast engineer George Galatis alleging the utility had compromised public safety during refueling shutdowns by removing more spent nuclear fuel than its federal license allowed.
The petition, supported by a Massachusetts consumer group, had asked that Northeast's license to operate the plant be revoked.
"It's not going to specifically suspend or revoke our license," Northeast spokesman Rich Gallagher said, referring to Thursday's ruling.

Neil Sheehan, a spokesman for the agency, said, "We've finally had a chance to look over the Galatis petition, which was one of the main sparks of this whole issue, and at least give him an answer on the technical issues. We still haven't given him an answer on the wrongdoing. That's pending."
Sheehan would not say when another ruling would come but said it was "unlikely" that Northeast's Millstone operating license would be revoked.
"Millstone is to the 1990s what Three Mile Island was to the '70s," Sheehan said in an interview.
"The scope of the problems is so widespread and so severe that Millstone has become symbolic of everything that's wrong with the nuclear industry."
The troubled utility's three Millstone nuclear plants have been closed for safety reasons since March.

Northeast said on Dec. 17 that it planned to have all three of the Millstone plants ready for restart by early 1998, pending approval by the regulatory agency. It did not say which plant would be ready first.
Northeast Utilities stock was unchanged at $12.75 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
